One day, Ben saw a shiny coin at the bottom of the pool. He wanted to get it, but it was too deep. He asked Mia for help.

"Mia, can you help me get the coin? It is very pretty and I value it a lot," he said.

Mia was thoughtful. She looked around and saw a drain near the pool. She had an idea.

"Ben, I have an idea. We can use the drain to make the water go away. Then we can get the coin," she said.

Ben liked the idea. He nodded and smiled. They worked together to move the pool near the drain. They opened the drain and watched the water go away. The coin was still there, shining in the sun.

"Wow, we did it! Thank you, Mia. You are very smart and kind," Ben said.

He gave Mia a hug and shared the coin with her. They were happy and proud. They learned that they could solve problems by being thoughtful and working together.

One night, after the old lady had finished her conversation, she noticed something very peculiar about the ashtray - it had started to move! In shock, the old lady yelled out to her friend, "What in the world is happening?"

Her friend replied, "The ashtray must be kind, because it wants you to be happy. It heard all the lovely things you said to me, and wanted to reward you with a dance!"

Once upon a time, there was a small green seed. The seed was small and round, and felt soft to the touch. The seed lay in the dirt, content to rest until something happened. 

Suddenly, a gust of wind blew through and the seed was swept up into the sky. The seed flew higher and higher until it reached a tree. At the top of the tree, the seed looked down and saw a long root. It was so deep that the seed could not see the end of it!

The seed tumbled and fell, down the root, deeper and deeper into the ground. The air was dark and damp, and the ground was soft. The seed felt safe and so it settled down. 

In the morning, the seed woke up to a bright blue sky. The tree was swaying in the wind and the root was swaying too! The seed was so happy, it wanted to join in the fun. It grabbed onto the root and started to swing! Up, down and round it went, feeling the wind in its leaves. 

The little seed continued to swing, high in the air. It felt free and alive, and nothing could stop its long swings. The seed remained swinging all day long, until the sun set, and the night came. 

The seed tucked itself away, safe and warm in the darkness, until the morning came and it could swing again.

completion:
One day George was walking along the beach looking for oysters. As he strolled, he noticed how the sand was a pale yellow color and the ocean was so clear he could see the many oyster shells. He eagerly started to pick up the oysters, hoping to find pearls inside them. 

When he had collected a few oysters, he heard a voice coming from behind him. He turned around to find an old man with a grey beard and a smile on his face. He said to George, "What are you doing, my child?" 

George proudly showed the the old man his collection and explained that he was looking for pearls inside the oysters. 

"That's very nice," said the old man, "But instead of increasing material possessions, it is better to increase your knowledge. With knowledge, you will always find the right answers." 

George thought about this for a moment and nodded. He thanked the old man for the advice, put the oysters back in the ocean, and wandered off home, thinking about what the old man had said. 

Moral of the story: Knowledge is more valuable than material possessions.

"Sorry, Mom," they say.

Mom sighs. She takes the tape and starts to unstick things.

"You should not play with tape. It is not a toy. It is for fixing things. You made a big mess. You should be embarrassed," she says.

Tom and Lily feel sad. They do not like to make Mom angry. They do not like to be embarrassed.

They hug Mom and say sorry again.

"Mom, we love you. We will not play with tape again. We will be good," they say.

Mom hugs them back. She is not angry anymore. She loves them too.

"It's okay. I forgive you. But next time, ask me before you use something. And help me clean up, please. You are my reliable kids," she says.

Tom and Lily nod. They help Mom clean up. They are happy again. They are still best friends.

"Who is that, Mama?" Anna asked, pointing at the lady.

"That is the bride, my dear. She is going to marry the prince today. They will have a big wedding at the castle," her mother explained.

Anna felt a pang of envy. She wished she could wear a veil and a dress like the bride. She wished she could go to the castle and see the prince. She wished she could be happy like the bride.

"Mama, can I have a veil too?" Anna asked.

Her mother smiled sadly and hugged her. "I'm sorry, my darling. We can't afford a veil. We barely have enough to eat. But you don't need a veil to be beautiful. You have a kind heart and a bright mind. That is more precious than any veil."

Anna nodded, but she still felt sad. She looked at the bride again and sighed.

"Maybe one day, Mama. Maybe one day."

"No, Tom, don't!" Sam said. He was wise. He knew snakes could bite. "Snakes are not toys. They can hurt you."

But Tom did not listen. He took a step closer to the snake. The snake saw him and hissed. It was angry. It raised its head and opened its mouth.

"Tom, stop!" Sam shouted. He was scared. He ran to Tom and pulled him back. The snake missed Tom by a hair. It slithered away into the bushes.

Tom was shocked. He started to cry. Sam hugged him and said, "It's okay, Tom. You are safe now. But you have to listen to me. I am your big brother. I know what is good for you."

Tom nodded. He said, "I'm sorry, Sam. You are right. You are wise. I will listen to you next time. Thank you for saving me."

Sam smiled. He said, "You're welcome, Tom. I love you. Come on, let's go home. Mom will make us some cookies."

They held hands and walked home. They learned a lesson. They never bothered snakes again.
